title: Corticosteroids before extubation in pediatric intensive care unit: a prospective randomized double-blind multicenter study
official: COBEX-PED  Corticosteroids before extubation in pediatric intensive care unit: a prospective randomized double-blind multicenter study
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of DXM-IV in reducing the incidence of DRPE/OVAS in children hospitalized in URP versus placebo
conditions: respiratory distress due to upper airway obstruction in child
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients intubated with an intubation tube with or without a cuff
2. o Peak inspiratory pressure ≤ 22 cmH2O or cough present
3. Full-term newborns, i.e., 37 weeks of amenorrhea (GA)+ 2 days until 6  years
4. Affiliated to a social security system
5. Collection of free and informed consent from parental authority, by both parents or by the legal guardian(s)
6. Under VM for at least 36 hours
7. And presenting the following extubation criteria:
8. o Extubation planned by the medical team,
9. o Inspired fraction of oxygen (FiO2) ≤ 45%
10. o Oxygen saturation measured by pulse oximeter ≥ 95% or appropriate depending on the pathology,
11. o Positive expiratory pressure (Pep) ≤ 8 cmH2O
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patient with a contraindication to DXM-IV:
2. o Current digestive hemorrhage
3. o Known hypersensitivity to DXM-IV or one of its excipients
4. Patient participating in another interventional research involving humans or being in the exclusion period following previous research involving humans, if applicable
5. Patient benefiting from State Medical Aid,
6. Premature newborn (<37 weeks of pregnancy)
7. Pre-existing corticosteroid therapy within 72 hours prior to randomization
8. Suffering from a known upper airway pathology (VAS) before intubation or at the time of extubation
9. History of VAS surgery in the month preceding inclusion
10. Any situation deemed incompatible with the child's participation in the trial is left to the free estimation of the investigating doctor
11. Decision to limit or stop treatments
12. o Uncontrolled local or general infection,
13. o Developing viruses (hepatitis, herpes, chickenpox, shingles),
14. o Live vaccines,
15. o Severe coagulation disorders,
